explanation: The Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is a powerful method used in molecular biology to amplify (make multiple copies of) a specific target sequence of DNA. This technique allows scientists to generate millions of copies of a single gene or DNA fragment inside a test tube. PCR requires a specialized DNA polymerase that is heat-stable and can withstand the high temperatures required to denature (separate) double-stranded DNA. The reaction also requires a supply of free nucleotides to build the new complementary strands. With each round of replication (cycle) in PCR, the total amount of target DNA doubles.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)?
opts: To degrade double-stranded DNA into single nucleotides.
To amplify a targeted sequence of DNA, creating millions of copies in a test tube.
To translate mature mRNA into active enzymes.
To splice exons together in alternative combinations.
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the slide states: PCR 'Amplifies (copies) a targeted sequence of DNA' and 'Creates millions of copies of a single gene or a specific piece of DNA in a test tube.' The other options are incorrect.

questions.q: Why is a heat-resistant DNA polymerase necessary for PCR?
opts: It prevents the DNA from winding around histone proteins.
It can withstand the high temperatures required to separate double-stranded DNA.
It converts RNA primers into DNA bases.
It degrades DNA templates that contain replication errors.
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the slide explains that PCR requires: 'DNA polymerase - Withstands the temperature necessary to separate double-stranded DNA.' The other options are incorrect.
